correctness.rationale: For the infinite cyclic group, every involutory anti-automorphism is one of the two automorphisms sending the generator to itself or its inverse. In the inversion branch, admissibility forces the central parameter to be the identity and Paiva Theorem 4.1 gives just-infiniteness. In the identity branch, the published multiplication rules yield the exact abelian presentation with relation u^2=a^k; Smith normal form gives Z plus a cyclic factor of order gcd(2,k), so just-infiniteness is equivalent to odd k.
risks: The result assumes the generalized Chein convention exactly as stated in arXiv:2609.21016v1; a different convention would require translating the parameter and involution notation.

value.rationale: The infinite cyclic group is the basic abelian just-infinite group, and all admissible generalized Chein triples over it can be exhausted without arbitrary parameter slicing. The result gives a complete answer to the first natural abelian test case of an explicit 2026 open question and identifies a sharp parity obstruction, including an infinite family where just-infiniteness of the base does not pass to the generalized double.
risks: The scope is intentionally the cyclic base case and does not by itself settle the general question.
